title: The One Partners In Health Clinic Not Built on Public Land
thinker: Jose, son of Jochanan, of Jerusalem (in Pirkei Avot)
conflicts: First clinic: Academy of Achievement says a two-room clinic opened in 1985; WBUR (2012) says a one-room clinic and ties it to 1987; Wikipedia says Zanmi Lasante was created in 1983. Story says 'a small clinic opened in the mid-1980s' and dates only Partners In Health's 1987 founding. Reach figures conflict (Kidder 2000: about a million rely on it, 100,000 in the catchment; Academy: more than 150,000; Wikipedia: 1.2 million) and are not used.
notes: Built on Farmer's own Academy of Achievement interview (2009), Kidder's New Yorker profile (2000) and Dahl and Farmer on WBUR (2012). The story spans 1983-1987 but stays on the one decision to build in Cange and the organisation formed to support it; the ending uses Dahl's later remark that the first clinic was the only one off public land. Stance 'complicates'. PIH's own pages, the NYT obituary and the eScholarship obituary are 403 to the verifier.
